newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia long bonds close at 2-1/2 yr peak.
newsitem.headline: Australia long bonds close at 2-1/2 yr peak.

text.p: *Australian bonds close firmer, with long bonds posting their best close in 2-1/2 years, while short end remains well below early highs after no rate cut appears.
*Curve closes at flattest level in one month

Australian 10-year bonds closed at their strongest levels since March 1994, while the short end also finished up on Wednesday but well below its early highs after the Reserve Bank did not announce a change in interest rates.
The market was bullish from the open after a strong performance by U.S. Treasuries overnight, with all the three December futures hitting contract highs early on.
The market was hoping for the RBA to announce a rate cut at 9.30 a.m. (2330 GMT) on Wednesday, and when it failed to eventuate bonds were sold off, most notably at the short end.

Bonds stabilised at the lower, but still positive levels, and late in the day long bonds received some support from Japanese investors as the Australian dollar/yen cross rate traded at four year highs, traders said.
December 10-year futures closed at 92.280, equal to last Friday's high, but slightly below the morning peak of 92.300.
The closing yield of 7.70 percent was the lowest close since the 7.67 percent recorded on March 25, 1994.
The three year contract opened above 93.00 and reached a peak of 93.03, also a 2-1/2 year high, but ran into profit taking and lost more lost ground when no rate cut eventuated.
A rate cut still remains well factored into the market, and was only seen as an outside chance for Wednesday morning.
Although the RBA can change rates on any day it chooses, most in the market expect it in either late October or early November.
Traders said attention now would return to the U.S., given the absence of any local data over the remainder of the week.
"The focus will now be on U.S. non-farm payrolls on Friday, with a local rate cut most likely to be after inflation and wages data later this month or the RBA meeting on November 5," one trader said.

After initially narrowing, short end spreads close weaker, while long end holds ground. Short end weakness sees the cash and futures curves flatten. The futures curves closes at its flattest level since September 6. NZ short end well supported by continuing samurai rumours.

After holding above 91.210 through the day, the 10-year contract firms to close at 91.280 resistance, which was also last week's high. Three years traded briefly above 93.00, but fell back and close under last week's high of 91.97.
